msContents.summary:
I) Introduction (fols. 2ra-8va) - Maqdǝma Wangel “Introduction to the Gospels” (fols. 2ra-7rc) - Letter of Eusebius to Carpianus (fol. 7rc l.19-8ra l.4) - “Synopsis of Classes” (fol. 8ra l.4-8va) II) Gospel of Matthew (fols. 11ra-61ra) - Bǝsrāta Mātewos “Gospel of Matthew” (fols. 11ra-60vb) - Postscript (fol. 61ra) III) Gospel of Mark (fols. 62ra-109rb) - Bǝsrāta Mārqos “Gospel of Mark” (fols. 62ra-87va) - Postscript (fol. 87vb) IV) Gospel of Luke (fols. 88ra-139ra) - Bǝsrāta Luqās (fols. 88ra-138vb) - Postscript (fol. 138vb-138ra) V) Gospel of John (fols. 142ra-180rb) - Bǝsrāta Yoḥannǝs “Gospel of John” (fols. 142ra-180ra) - Postscript (fol. 180ra)
Additiones 1-3.

handDesc.handNote: Fairly careful Black, red; reddish-brown. Scribe: Ḫāyla ʾIyasus. Ḫāyla ʾIyasus is mentioned as the scribe in supplication formulas (11r, 62r, 142r).Late 19th century Nomina sacra; incipits and headings of the texts; numbers of the chapters and the word mǝʿrāf or its abbreviation; elements of the punctuation signs and Ethiopic numerals. Reddish-brown ink is used for rubrication in fols. 176ra-180rb.
Broad, rounded letters' forms. The script size is larger in 88r-130v.

decoDesc.decoNote: Fol. 9v: St. Michael with the donors Tawalda Madḫǝn and Walatta Madḫǝn.Legend in the upper margin: ዘከመ፡ ተሰየመ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ኅበ፡ እግዚአብሔር, “How St. Michael was appointed by God“ Legend in the upper left corner: ዘከመ፡ ተማኅፀነ፡ ባህር፡ ነጋሢ፡ ተወልደ፡ መድኅን, “How bāhr nagāśi Tawalda Madḫǝn entrusted himself”. Legend in the lower margin: ዘከመ፡ ተማኅፀነት፡ ወይዘሮ፡ ድንቁ፡ ወለተ፡ መድኅን, “How wäyzäro Dǝnqu Walatta Madḫǝn entrusted herself”.
Fol. 10r: St. Matthew the Evangelist.Legend: ዘብእሲ፡ ማቴዎስ, “Matthew of the (winged) man”.
Fol. 61v: St. Mark the Evangelist.Legend: ዘአንበሳ፡ ማርቆስ, “Mark of the (winged) lion”, frontispiece miniature.
Fol. 139v: St. Luke the Evangelist.Legend: ዘላህም፡ ሉቃስ, “Luke of the (winged) ox”.
Fol. 140r: St. John the Evangelist.Legend: ዘንስር፡ ዮሐንስ, “John of the eagle”.

Fol. 140v: The donor Tawalda Madḫǝn with mamhǝr Takla Libānos and soldiers.Legend in the upper left margin: መምህር፡ ተክለ፡ ሊባኖስ, “Mämhǝr Takla Libānos”. Legend in the upper right margin: ዘከመ፡ ተዋነየ፡ ምስለ፡ ፍቁራኒሁ፡ ባህር፡ ነጋሢ፡ ተወልደ፡ መድኅን, “How bāhr nagāśi Tawalda Madḫǝn is conversing with his beloved ones”.

Fol. 141r: The donor Tawalda Madḫǝn, guided by the Angel, and his soldiers.Legend: ወይመርሖ፡ መላክ፡ ፋኖተ (sic!)፡ እንተኃረየ፡ ወነፋሱሂ(sic!)፡ ውስተ፡ ሠናይ፡ ተኃድር, “And the Angel leads him the way that he has chosen and his soul into peaceful rest”.

From the beginning till the word ፯ወለደ, it is written in black ink in the same hand as the legends of the miniatures. An identical genealogy of baḥr nagāśi Tawalda Madḫǝn, written in the same hand, appears in Ms. UM-029. The remaining part of the note is written in a different hand which explains why it is missing from UM-029 (in that Ms. only one of his daughters is mentioned, 84vb 31 ).

item.desc: : Record concerning a dispute over the lands between ʿUra and ʾAgärhǝse.
item.note: The note, written in Tǝgrǝñña, states the result of the court case, the two parties involved, the witnesses and the decision-makers.
The note has been partly erased. It mentions the wife of the donor and other members of his family. It ends with a condemnation formula.

list.item:
- Tituli of the chapters are written in the upper margins: e.g., 18r, 23v, 29v, 38r, 53r. - Name of a qes gabaz crudely written in pencil: 180v, 181r. - Ṭälsäm (talisman) picture crudely drawn in pencil: 181r. - Crude minor notes in pen and pencil: 1rv, 9r, 91r.
- The miniatures are painted by the same illuminator as in UM-029. Also, the legends are written in the same hand as that of UM-029.

item.desc: - The beginning and the end of the daily reading is marked by a line, e.g., fol. 86rb. - Readings are indicated by the names of the feasts and other occasions crudely written in the upper margin, in pen: e.g. fols. 12v, 13v, 14r.

binding.decoNote: Two wooden boards covered with dark brown tooled leather (the back board is broken and repaired with cord). Two pairs of sewing stations.
Two pairs of chains of endband stitches at the spine cover. Separate pieces of reddish-brown leather were used to repair or strengthen the spine.
Blind tooled ornament on the dark brown leather cover (at least 6 tools were used: triple line fillet, double sine wave with dots, cross hatching, double circle, cherckerboard, wave form).

origin.origDate: Baḥr nagāśi Tawalda Madḫǝn donated also Ms. UM-029, dated to the time of King Yoḥannǝs IV (r. 1872-1889) and Metropolitan Ṗeṭros IV (in tenure 1881-1917).

history.provenance: Tawalda Madḫǝn is mentioned as the donor in the supplication formulas on 11r, 62r, 88r (together with his wife Walatta Madḫǝn), 142r and 180rb; his name is written in the same hand as Additio 1 and the legends of the miniatures. His title, bahr nagāśi, is mentioned in Additio 1 and in the legend of miniatures 1 and 6.
